thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: Elevated 5xx + timeouts observed for inference-scheduler across us-west-2 (error spike at 12:04 UTC). Paging oncall. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/scheduler-backpressure :rotating_light:

maria (oncall): on it. seeing the page. pulling metrics now.

mar ia (oncall): ack (typo) — sorry. metrics: controller queue length climbing, scheduler latency p95 jumped from 60ms -> 1.2s, 5xx rate ~6% overall but 18% for long-context model variant.

tom (sre): can you paste the top error type? gateway timeout vs downstream 5xx?

maria (oncall): logs show a mix: upstream gateway timeouts and internal 500s from worker process OOM in a few hosts. head-of-line blocking in the batching queue — a few long-context requests holding KV cache and preventing normal small requests from batching.

alex (prod-eng): repro hypothesis: large ctx requests allocate large KV sets and dominate slot scheduling -> continuous batching backpressure. Are those requests from a single customer?

maria (oncall): quick filter on request headers shows ~60% of the long-context inflight came from customer: "bigchat.ai" (customer id: c-984).

customer-ops: flagged bigchat.ai via alerting earlier — UX team already got a slack DM. We should prepare a status note.

maria (oncall): mitigation plan step 1: reduce scheduler batch window for affected pods, step 2: offload long-context traffic to fallback small-model variant, step 3: hotspot mitigation: cordon + restart OOM hosts. executing now.

deploy-bot: @maria (oncall) triggered config change: scheduler.batch_window -> 15ms on cluster scheduler-prod-usw2. Change id: cfg-20260323-1.

maria (oncall): applied cfg-20260323-1 to 30% of scheduler pods in canary pool. observing metrics...

(45s later)

maria (oncall): canary looks promising: overall queue depth dropped 40% on canaries, p95 latency improved ~300ms. 5xx rate down in canaries to 2.2% from 8%.

alex (prod-eng): moving to step 2: add routing rule to push requests with ctx_len > 12k to model-compact-v2 (quantized) and set a soft 10rps cap for that route. Doing canary first.

tom (sre): whole-cluster scale: can we spin up extra scheduler workers to drain backlog? autoscaler currently maxed; propose temporary manual scale + add headroom.

maria (oncall): manual scale +3 scheduler replicas in us-west-2: command run: `kubectl scale deployment/scheduler --replicas=+3 -n inference-prod-usw2` -> deploy-bot confirms scale job queued.

deploy-bot: Scale job started: job-id scale-1769125128. Expected replica count change: +3.

(2m later)

maria (oncall): scaling rolled; new pods coming up, but a few older pods still showing OOM loops. I've cordoned the worst offenders: `kubectl annotate node node-12 cordoned-by=oncall-1769125000` and filed a ticket to infra to root cause OOM.

jay (oncall-next): pinged — I'll take handoff once we get to steady-state. oncall-next standing by.

maria (oncall): customer impact summary for comms: ~6% global requests affected during peak, top affected customers: bigchat.ai (~52% of long-ctx errors), partner-x (~8%), others small. Degraded responses were timeouts and 500s; median latency for small-context requests increased but returned to baseline in canary.

customer-ops: preparing status update to bigchat.ai: short note with ETA ~30m for mitigation and offer to replay buffered requests if needed.

alex (prod-eng): after routing change + scale, I'm seeing sustained reduced queue length. We're still seeing occasional spikes tied to a sub-second batch that still hogs KV. I recommend a targeted throttling rule: reject new long-ctx requests with 429 when queue depth > 5000 for the cluster. I'll open PR to add that safeguard to router.

maria (oncall): agree. temp throttling until we have a long-term scheduling fix. Filed PR #5784 and applied feature-flag `throttle-long-ctx-v0` to canary.

(10m later)

maria (oncall): metrics steady, 5xx reduced to ~1.1%, timeouts back to baseline. cordoned nodes quarantined for postmortem.

tom (sre): good work. next steps: postmortem triage, runbook updates (add throttle threshold + model-routing mitigation), and customer follow-ups. Please ensure all actions + config diffs are linked in the postmortem.

maria (oncall): starting a brief incident summary for the postmortem. handoff to jay in 20.

jay (oncall-next): taking over. I have the logs and runbook links. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: error rates returned to normal. Incident duration: 00:42:40. Incident ID: INC-2026-3147. Please fill the postmortem template: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-3147/postmortem

maria (oncall): adding notes: root cause likely scheduler queue head-of-line blocking from disproportionate long-context requests + insufficient throttling. Next actions: enforce long-ctx routing by default, add autoscaler buffer, update runbook thresholds.

customer-ops: sent update to bigchat.ai with apology and mitigation summary.

alex (prod-eng): will follow up with infra about OOMs and with runtime team about more graceful eviction for large-KV requests.

jay (oncall-next): acknowledged handoff. Closing thread for now.
